exposure: mode of delivery (cesarean section vs. normal spontaneous delivery)
outcome: Prevalence of vitamin D deficiency in infants and mothers
Levels of calcium, phosphorus, and 25(OH) vitamin D
cohort: 2,460 infants admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit of Afiyet Hospital in Turkey between August 2014 and January 2018
finding: There was a statistically significant positive correlation between vitamin D levels in mothers and their infants (78.7%, p: 0.000, p<0.05).
mod_finding: This study found that infants born via cesarean section (C/S) had higher rates of vitamin D deficiency compared to infants born via Normal Spontaneous Delivery (NSD).
